Indian Standard SPECIFICATION FOR ELECTRIC H A N D - L A M P S ( Revised )
0. F O R E W O R D 0.1 This Indian Standard ( Revised ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 May 1966, after the draft finalized by the Electrical Appliances Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electiotcchnical Division Council. 0.2 This standard covers portable hand-lamps ( also known as Inspection lamps) with a body and handle incorporating lampholder, guard and strap, hook or other devices, but not including the lamps. Thi$ standard does not cover special types of hand-lamps, such as gastight, flameproof, watertight, or dustproof hand-lamps, as well as portable lamp stands and brackets. 0.3 This standard covers the general, safety and performance requirements of electric hand-lamps to ensure reliable operation, personal safety against electric shock and safety against the effects of excessive temperature and fire. 0.4 This standard was originally published in 1959. It has been revised with a view to: a) aligning it with IS : 302-1973*; and b) specifying additional requirements and test procedures, for example, requirements and tests for temperature limit, creepage distances and clearances, screws and connections, fire resisting properties, etc, and details on sampling procedure for acceptance. 0.4.1 The special requirements of tropical countries like India as well as the testing facilities at the disposal of light electrical appliances industry in the country have been taken into consideration while preparing this revision. 0.5 IS : 302-1973* to which references have been made in this standard with regard to general and safety requirements as well as methods of tests is a necessary adjunct to this standard. Should, however, any deviation exist between the requirements of IS : 302-1973* and those of this standard, provisions of latter shall apply.
* General and safety requirements for household and similar electrical appliances (fourth revision).

3

IS : 1415 - 1966 0.6 While preparing this specification, assistance has been derived from the following: No. C. 118-1957 Ap. SAA Approval and test specification for electric hand-lamps. Standards Association of Australia. B.S. 1980 : 1953 Portable electric hand-lamps (open type with protective guard ). British Standards Institution. 0.7 This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on domestic and light electrical appliances. A list of standards published so far in this series is given on 4th cover. 0.8 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with I S : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 1 . SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the requirements and methods of tests for electric portable hand-lamps for use on supply voltages not exceeding 250 volts single phase ac or dc, and suitable for use with lamps having wattages not exceeding 150 W. 1.1.1 Special types of hand-lamps like flameproof, gastight, watertight or dustproof hand-lamps are excluded from the scope of this standard. 1.1.2 This standard does not also cover portable lampstands and brackets. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the definition given in 2.1 shall apply in addition to those specified in 2 of IS : 302-1973. 2.1 H a n d - L a m p -- A portable electric-light fitting suitable for carrying in hand. It consists of a body, handle, a lampholder (excluding a lamp), guard and strap or hook or other device for suspension or carrying. It does not include portable lampstands, brackets and similar fittings of a decorating nature although they may be movable and not fixed. 3. RATING 3.1 Voltage Rating -- The preferred voltages shall be 240, 24, 12 and 6 V.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( wised).  General and safety requirements for household and similar electrical appliances (fourth revision).

4

IS : 1415 - 1966 4. MATERIALS 4.1 The relevant provisions of 7.11 and 7.12 of I S : 302-1973* shall apply in addition to those specified in 4.2 to 4.7 of this standard. 4.2 Body and Handle -- The body and handle of the hand-lamp shall be made of suitably treated hardwood or other suitable non-hygroscopic insulating material capable of withstanding rough usage and the heat generated by the lamp* The materials used shall be such that it shall not be uncomfortable to hold the handle. 4.2.1 There shall be at least 10 cm of clear gripping space on the handle. 4.2.2 The following precautions shall be taken to ensure that it is impossible for a screw or other non-current-carrying metal part to act as a conductor from the inside to the outside of the body or handle: a) Any metal screw or fixing entering the body from the outside shall not penetrate within 4 mm of the inner wall of the cavity in the centre of the body. b) Any metal screw or fixing in contact with an interior metal part entering the body from the inside shall not penetrate within 4 mm from the outer surface. c) If any metal screw or fixing inserted from the inside of the body projects to the outside for the purpose, for instance, of securing an external metal part, the head shall be recessed into the body by at least 4 mm clear and, in addition, shall be permanently shrouded in such a manner as to exclude the possibility of electrical contact with any interior metal part. 4.3 Guard and Shield 4.3.1 The guard shall be of suitable design and of adequate strength to provide adequate protection for the lamp and lampholder and to provide a convenient base on which to stand the hand-lamp. The guard may be open at the end. The guard, if of metal, shall be separated from the metal parts of the lampholder and from any metal parts in contact therewith by proper insulation. 4.3.2 When required, a shield to obscure the light in the desired directions may be fitted inside or outside the guard. The shield, if fitted, shall be arranged so as not to make contact with the lampholder or lamp. 4.3.3 The guard shall be so designed as to provide easy means of lamp replacement preferably without necessitating the removal of the guard from the body. 4.4 Switches -- Hand-lamps shall not be provided with a switch.
*General and safety requirements for household and similar electrical appliances (fourth revision).

5

IS : 1415 - 1966 4.5 Bushes or Bellmonth Ends -- The hole through which the flexible cord or cable enters the body of the hand-lamp shall be of bellmouth type or so shaped as to prevent or avoid the abrasion of the conductor or its insulation which may lead to its electrical or mechanical failure. Bushes, if used, shall be securely fixed in position. 4.6 Hanging Device -- Every hand-lamp shall be provided with a or hook by means of which it may be hung up when not in use. such device for independent suspension shall be securely attached shall be so positioned that it is not capable of penetrating the guard causing breakage of the lamp.
NOTE -- In no case shall the lamp be meant to be suspended on its flexible cord.

loop Any and and

4.7 Lampholder -- The lampholdcr shall be suitable for the voltage and wattage rating of the lamp used in the hand-lamp. If of bayonet type, it shall comply with the requirements of IS : 1258-1958*. It shall be easy to wire and shall be secured in such a manner that neither longitudinal nor circumferential movement is possible when the lamp is inserted or removed. Such fixing shall be independent of the clamping action of any detachable guard. 5. CONSTRUCTION 5.1 The relevant provisions of 7 of IS : 302-1973 shall apply. 6. GENERAL AND SAFETY REQUIREMENTS 6.1 Protection Against Electric Shock -- The provisions of 8 of IS : 302-1973 shall apply. 6.2 Temperature Limit -- The provisions of Table 3 of IS : 302-1973 shall apply. 6.3 Electric Insulation -- The provisions of 11 of I S : 302-1973 shall apply. 6.4 Moisture Resistance -- The provisions of 13 of IS : 3C2-1973 shall apply. 6.5 Mechanical Strength-- The provisions of 15 of I S : 302-1973 shall apply. 6.6 Supply Connections -- T h e provisions of 20 of IS : 302-1973 shall apply, except that the length of service cord shall be 5 m. 6.7 Terminals -- The provisions of 21 of IS : 302-1973 shall apply.
* Specification for bayonet lampholders. Generaf and safety requirements for household and similar electrical appliances (fourth revision).

6

IS : 1415 - 1966 6.8 Provisions of Earthing -- The provisions of 22 of IS : 302-1973* shall apply. 6.9 Screws and Connections -- The provisions of 23 of IS : 302 - 1973* shall apply. 6.10 Resistance to Rusting -- T h e provisions of 7.33 of IS : 302 - 1973* shall apply in case of metal parts like handle, guard and shield, etc. 7. MARKING AND INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE 7.1 Each hand-lamp shall be marked indelibly and clearly with the following particulars: a) Name or trade-mark of the manufacturer, b) Rated voltage and the maximum wattage of the lamp that could be used, c) Makers model or type reference, and d) Country of manufacture. 7.1.1 The hand-lamps may also be marked with the ISI Certification Mark.
N O T E -- T h e use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered bv an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. ISI marked products are also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

7.2 Marking of the Earth Terminal -- The symbol marked permanently on or adjacent to the earth terminal.

shall be

7.3 Instructions for Use -- Each hand-lamp shall be provided with necessary instructions including precautions to be taken for its use. 8. TESTS 8.1 Categories of Tests 8.1.1 Type Tests -- The tests given in Table I shall constitute type tests and shall be carried out on five samples of electric hand-lamps of the same type, model and ratings (selected preferably at random from a regular production lot). 8.1.1.1 Criteria of acceptance -- All samples shall successfully pass all the type tests for proving conformity with the requirements of this standard.
*General and safety requirements for household ( fourth revision ). and similar electrical appliances

7

IS : 1415 - 1966 If any of the samples fail in any of the type tests, testing authority at its discretion may call for fresh samples not exceeding twice the original number and subject them again to all tests or to the test(s) in which failure(s) occurred. No single failure shall be permitted in the repeat test(s). 8.1.2 Acceptance Tests -- The following shall constitute acceptance tests:

8.3.2 Test for Mechanical Strength -- The hand-lamps shall be allowed to fall six times vertically from a height of 30 cm on to a wooden floor or solid wooden bench. 8.3.2.1 T h e r e shall be no d a m a g e to the handle and guard which affects the working of the lamp and no points shall be broken or cracked. 8.3.3 Test for Temperature Limit -- T h e h a n d - l a m p shall be connected to a source of supply of maximum rated voltage until stable temperatures are reached. For the purpose of this test the hand-lamp shall be fitted with lamp of the largest wattage which could be used in normal service. T h e temperature of any material or insulation or operating part shall not exceed the limits given in T a b l e 3 of IS : 302-1973*.

APPENDIX A ( Clause 8.1.2.1 )
SAMPLING P R O C E D U R E FOR ACCEPTANCE A-1. LOT A-1.1 In any consignment, all electric hand-lamps of the same make, model and type, and manufactured under similar conditions of production shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. *General and safety requirements for household and similar electrical appliances ( fourth revision ). 9

SELECTION OF SAMPLE A-2.1 From each lot a certain number of electric hand-lamps, as prescribed in Table 2, shall be selected at random and subjected to the tests specified in 8.1.2. A-2.2 The number of electric hand-lamps to be selected from the lot shall depend upon the size of the lot and shall be in accordance with col 2 of Table 2 . A-2.2.1 If required for repeat tests (see A-3.2), additional number of hand-lamps, as given in col 3 of Table 2, shall be selected at random.

A-3. CRITERION FOR CONFORMITY A-3.1 The lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements of acceptance tests if the number of failures in the first sample is less than or equal to acceptance number Cl, as given in col 4 of Table 2. If the number of failures is greater than or equal to the rejection number C2, as given in col 5 of Table 2, the lot shall be considered as not conforming to the requirements of the acceptance tests. A-3.2 If the number of failures is between C1 and C2, a further sample of N2 electric hand-lamps shall be selected and subjected to the acceptance tests. If the number of failures in the two samples combined is less than C2, the lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements of the acceptance tests, otherwise not.
